title: Godfather Trojan Investigation
description: Investigate the Godfather Android banking Trojan in your network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The Godfather Android banking Trojan has been detected in your network. This trojan is designed to harvest login credentials for banking applications and other financial services, and drain the accounts. It uses web fakes to overlay on infected devices that appear when a user interacts with a decoy notification or tries to open one of the legitimate applications targeted by Godfather. Any data entered on the web fakes is exfiltrated to command-and-control (C&C) servers. Godfather can also exfiltrate SMS and push notifications to bypass two-factor authentication.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have access to the victim host `victim` with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. You can also access the C2 server `c2-server` with the same credentials. To proceed to the next level, enter the word 'start'.
levels.local_content: You have access to the victim host `victim` with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. You can also access the C2 server `c2-server` with the same credentials. To proceed to the next level, enter the word 'start'.

levels.title: Identify the suspicious scheduled task/timer used by the Godfather trojan
levels.content: Investigate the systemd timers on the victim host to find any suspicious scheduled tasks that might be related to the Godfather trojan. Look for a timer named `GoogleProtect.timer`. The flag type is a string.
levels.solution: Use the systemctl command to list all timers and look for any that seem out of place. The command `systemctl list-timers` will display all active timers.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Systemd timers are used to schedule tasks. Malicious timers often have unusual names.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the systemctl command to list all timers and look for any that seem out of place.

levels.title: Identify the hidden malware directory used by the Godfather trojan
levels.content: Search the victim host for any hidden directories that might be used by the Godfather trojan to store its files. Look for a hidden directory named `/var/lib/.netd`. The flag type is a string.
levels.solution: Use the find command to search for hidden directories across the filesystem. The command `find / -type d -name '.*' 2>/dev/null` will list all hidden directories.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Malware often hides in directories with unusual names or locations.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the find command to search for hidden directories across the filesystem.

levels.title: Identify the attacker-controlled C2 server
levels.content: Investigate the network connections on the victim host to find any suspicious outbound connections to a command-and-control (C&C) server. Look for the IP address `192.168.60.20`. The flag type is an IP address.
levels.solution: Use the ss command to list all network connections and look for any suspicious outbound connections. The command `ss -tulnp` will display all active network connections.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Malware often communicates with external command-and-control servers.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use the ss command to list all network connections and look for any suspicious outbound connections.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: The IP address of the C2 server is `192.168.60.20`.
